_comment: Copy to config.json and fill in client_id / client_secret from https://develop.battle.net/access/clients . Keys starting with _ are documentation and are ignored. Secrets can instead go in the BNET_CLIENT_ID / BNET_CLIENT_SECRET environment variables, which override this file. config.json itself is gitignored - do not commit it.
_professions: Empty list = all of them. Narrowing this is the single biggest speed-up for `init`.
_skill_tiers: Substring match on the skill tier name; empty list = every expansion back to Classic. Left empty deliberately: `init` caches the lot once (~15 min) and `scan` is then free to score any slice of it, so narrow a single run with --tier instead of narrowing the cache. Old tiers are also the trustworthy ones - they still publish crafted_item and rarely use reagent slots, unlike Midnight. Verified 2026-08-13 (patch 12.1.0): current tiers are all named 'Midnight <Profession>', so --tier Midnight matches them all.
_addon_path: Where the WowCraftExport addon lives. `scan` writes PriceData.lua here so reagent tooltips and the crafting window show prices in game. /reload to pick up a new one.
_history_days: Days of price history to keep. One row per item per day; several scans on the same day update that day's row. 0 keeps everything. This is also the window the smoothed sell price and the sale rate are measured over, so shortening it makes both twitchier.
_cover_days: How many days of stock the Craft column aims to cover. Short is deliberate: an undercut war or a patch should not catch you holding a month of inventory. --cover-days overrides it for one run.
_market_share: The fraction of an item's daily volume you assume you take. 0 works it out per item as 1 / (listings + 1) - you as one more seller among those already posted, so a crowded market promises you less. Set it to e.g. 0.25 to use a flat share instead.
_demand_cap_turnover: Caps a measured sale rate at this many times the item's standing supply per day. The rate counts a cancelled auction as a sale and cannot do otherwise, so on thinly-listed items holding big stacks the undercut churn dominates - live data had one mat claiming ten turnovers a day. 1 leaves the honest 93% of items untouched; 0 disables the cap.
_sale_basis: Which sale signal the rate is built on. "likely" counts every auction that vanished with hours still to run - it cannot have expired, but it can have been cancelled. "swept" counts only the ones that went from below the cheapest listing that survived the interval, which is what a buyer eating up the ladder can account for, so undercut churn drops out. Both are recorded on every scan either way; this only picks which one the ranking reads. The scan prints the gap between them - watch it for a few days before switching.
_price_basis: "market" smooths the sell price across the stored days, weighted towards recent ones - a single scan is one moment, and one seller undercutting for an hour should not become the price. "current" uses this scan's reading alone, which is what the tool did before. Only the sell side is ever smoothed: reagents are bought at today's asking prices off the live ladder.
_pull_url: Where `pull` fetches a published scan from - the GitHub Pages site the hourly workflow deploys to, e.g. https://<user>.github.io/wow-craft-margins/ . Set this and this machine needs no credentials, no recipe cache and no scheduled scan; `pull` just downloads the answer. Empty = this PC scans for itself.
_dispatch: GitHub's scheduler is best-effort and drops slots. If the published data is older than dispatch_when_stale_minutes, `pull` asks GitHub to run the scan now rather than waiting out the gap. Blizzard refreshes hourly, so past 90 minutes a cycle went missing rather than merely running late. 0 disables the whole thing and needs no token.
_github_token: A FINE-GRAINED token, this repository only, with Actions: read and write and nothing else. Prefer the WOWCRAFT_GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable, which overrides this - config.json is gitignored, but a token in an environment variable cannot be committed by accident at all. Leave empty to never dispatch.
_dispatch_repo: "owner/name". Empty = derived from pull_url when that is a project Pages URL; set it for a custom domain.
_dispatch_wait_seconds: How long to wait for the requested scan to publish before leaving it to the next pull. A run takes about a minute plus the Pages deploy. 0 = do not wait.
